title: Audit session linker: admin-scoped search, CSV/JSON export, and session correlation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Admins need a way to investigate user sessions end-to-end: from SSO/SAML authentication to API activity and console actions. Current audit viewer shows event streams but it is hard to group events by session or SAML assertion, and exports do not respect RBAC v2 scoping for admin delegates. This ticket implements a session-linker feature that surfaces correlated events, provides admin-scoped saved searches, and enables secure CSV/JSON exports with row-level redaction governed by RBAC v2 policies.

Scope: UI changes to search/filter panel (new 'Session ID' and 'SSO Assertion ID' facets), backend event-join service to stitch events by session token and SAML assertion, export endpoints supporting streaming JSONL and chunked CSV with cursors, RBAC-aware redaction middleware using customer KMS keys optionally, and saved-query persistence for organizations with role-based visibility.
acceptance_criteria: Admins can enter or click a Session ID or SSO Assertion ID to see a timeline of correlated events (console, API, SSO) within the viewer
Export endpoints produce CSV and JSONL matching the filtered view and apply RBAC redaction rules (PII masked for non-authorized roles)
Large exports (>10M rows) stream via cursor-based paging and support resume from last cursor token
Saved searches that include session/SSO facets can be saved and shared with org-level visibility rules enforced by RBAC v2
Audit viewer pagination remains responsive under typical customer load (95th latencies < 500ms for paginated slices)
design_feedback: Design prefers an inline timeline card for session detail rather than a separate pane to reduce context switching
Show a privacy indicator on export modal when redaction is applied and link to RBAC policy editor
Use condensed chips for session/SSO facets and allow compound facet pinning to saved queries
engineering_notes: Backend will add an event_correlation service that consumes audit events and writes session index records to a time-series index (TTL 90 days by default)
We will extend existing export job framework to support streaming JSONL and cursor tokens; reuse chunked uploader used for activity-archive
RBAC v2 integration: use permission evaluation at export time to decide per-field redaction. This requires lightweight policy cache on export workers to avoid a DB hop per row
KMS integration required for customer-managed redaction keys; will call KMS only for first-row key unwrap and cache DEKs per job
We need to be careful about correlating SAML assertion IDs across identity providers where assertion formats vary — normalization layer required
blockers: RBAC policy cache implementation (ENG-70400) is not complete; blocks safe, low-latency redaction checks
KMS access for test tenants: security needs to provision test keys for on-prem and cloud flows before export redaction can be validated
Telemetry quotas: the session index writer will increase write QPS to our metrics cluster; infra review required (ENG-71112)
changes_requested: PM requested a configuration toggle to disable session correlation for customers who do not want cross-service linkage
Security requested an explicit consent flag in export modal for customer-managed KMS key usage
Design asked that saved-query visibility be explicit (Org, Team, Private) and default to 'Team' for non-admin creators
deployment_plan: Feature rollout in three phases: 1) backend event index + RBAC redaction prototype behind feature flag (dev orgs), 2) UI session timeline + saved-query UX to a subset of customers for feedback, 3) wide release with streaming export enabled. Each phase gated by automated E2E tests and targeted perf tests. Monitor export worker CPU and KMS QPS for 72 hours post-release.
notes: 2026-02-26: Spike completed to evaluate correlation performance; median extra latency for timeline queries ~40ms when using session index
2026-03-03: Security review kickoff, initial concerns about cross-tenant leakage addressed by strict org-scoping in session index keys
2026-03-08: Design review accepted timeline card after minor copy tweaks; PM approved scope with feature flags
2026-03-10: Backend PR opened for event correlator (link above), running integration tests against staging export cluster
